evidence.quote: Take this time to Frogfucius in Tadpole Pond and he will give you the Frog Coins as thanks.

facts.subject: Frog Coin grinding
facts.text: In Land's End, the whirlpools of sand have an ant; jumping on it with good timing nets 20 Coins and 1 Frog Coin per complete cycle.

evidence.quote: With good timing, you can jump on the ant that appears inside the whirlpools, netting 20 Coins and 1 Frog Coin for a complete cycle.

facts.subject: Frog Coin grinding
facts.text: Replaying the Paratroopa Cliff Scaling game after first scaling the cliff, with a time of 12 seconds or lower, nets a Frog Coin.

evidence.quote: The second method is simply by replaying the Paratroopa Cliff Scaling game anytime after you scale the cliff for the first time. Scoring a time of 12 seconds or lower will net you a Frog Coin.

facts.subject: Forest Maze Wiggler Frog Coin
facts.text: In Forest Maze rooms with stumps, Wigglers pop in and out of the stumps; hopping onto one without triggering a fight and staying for ten jumps gives a Frog Coin.

evidence.quote: In rooms with stumps, there are usually Wigglers popping in and out of the stumps. If you can hop onto one without triggering a fight and stay on him for ten jumps, you'll get a Frog Coin.

facts.subject: Forest Maze Wiggler Frog Coin
facts.text: The Wiggler method is easily repeatable and much safer than the ants in the whirlpools.

evidence.quote: This is easily repeatable and much safer than the ants in the whirlpools.

facts.subject: Ghost coin grinding
facts.text: A quick way to obtain lots of Coins is to fight ghost-type monsters like the Boos in Kero Sewers.

evidence.quote: A quick way to obtain lots of Coins is to fight ghost-type monsters (like the Boos in Kero Sewers, for example).

facts.subject: Pure Water
facts.text: Defeating ghost enemies gives Pure Water, an item that can insta-kill any ghost-type enemies.

evidence.quote: Each time you defeat ghost enemies, you receive Pure Water, an item that can insta-kill any ghost-type enemies.

facts.subject: Pure Water
facts.text: Pure Waters are easily grindable and sell for 75 coins apiece.

evidence.quote: Pure Waters are easily grindable and sell for 75 coins apiece

facts.subject: Super Jump items
facts.text: In Monstro Town, enter the second door on the left; the Chow in this building tracks how many Super Jumps you land on enemies.

evidence.quote: In Monstro Town, enter the second door on the left. The Chow in this building will keep track of how many Super Jumps you land on enemies.

facts.subject: Super Jump
facts.text: Super Jump is learned by Mario at level 6.

evidence.quote: Super Jump is learned by Mario at level 6.

facts.subject: Super Jump timing
facts.text: The timing shifts at around jump #18, but otherwise it is fairly consistent once you get going.

evidence.quote: The timing shifts at around jump #18, but otherwise it's fairly consistent to keep landing hits once you get going.

facts.subject: Super Jump limit
facts.text: You automatically hop off an enemy if you hit 100 jumps.

evidence.quote: You will automatically hop off an enemy if you hit 100 jumps.

facts.text: After 30 Super Jumps, talking to the Chow gives the Attack Scarf, an accessory that greatly boosts Attack Power and can be worn by anyone.

evidence.quote: After you achieve 30 Super Jumps, talk to the Chow to obtain the Attack Scarf, an accessory which greatly boosts Attack Power and can be worn by anyone.

facts.subject: Super Suit
facts.text: After 100 Super Jumps, talking to the Chow again gives the Super Suit, one of Mario's best armors.

evidence.quote: After 100 Super Jumps, talk to the Chow again and he'll give you the Super Suit, one of Mario's best armors.

facts.subject: Fertilizer

evidence.quote: You'll find the Shy Away again, who will gladly give you the Fertilizer in exchange for letting him live.

facts.text: With both the Seed and Fertilizer, go to Rose Town, take the northeast exit to a section with a single house, and speak to the farmer inside.

facts.text: Hand the Seed and Fertilizer to the farmer; he plants the Seed in the giant pot and fertilizes it, making a large vine sprout through his chimney into the sky.

facts.subject: Lazy Shell

evidence.quote: Climb this vine to the top. You'll be in the clouds, where two chests containing the Lazy Shell weapon and armor await you.

facts.subject: Jinx

evidence.quote: In Monstro Town, climb the stairs near the Save Block to a door with a sign hanging outside painted with a "J".

facts.subject: Jagger
facts.text: Jagger is not too difficult; just keep pressure on him.

evidence.quote: Jagger isn't too difficult, just keep pressure on him and you'll have no trouble

facts.subject: Jinx
facts.text: Jinx has average health but his attacks either deal high damage or are essentially one-hit KOs.

evidence.quote: Jinx has an average amount of health compared to most bosses, but the real danger is his attacks, which either deal high damage or are essentially one-hit KOs

facts.subject: Jinx
facts.text: Having the Lazy Shell armor on a healer such as Peach helps a lot if you tackle Jinx right when you reach Monstro Town.

evidence.quote: Having the Lazy Shell armor on a healer character (Peach is a good choice) helps a lot

facts.subject: Jinx
facts.text: Geno Boost helps punch through Jinx's high physical defense, and NT220 notes Jinx is susceptible to Jump attacks.

evidence.quote: Geno's Geno Boost can also help punch through his high physical defense stat. NT220 of the GameFAQs message boards also notes that Jinx is susceptible to Jump attacks.

facts.subject: Jinx
facts.text: Jinx must be defeated three times, gaining more HP and defense each time, before he acknowledges Mario as the true dojo master.

evidence.quote: Once you defeat Jinx three times (he gains more HP and defense each time), he'll acknowledge Mario as the true dojo master.

facts.subject: Jinx Belt
facts.text: The Jinx Belt boosts a character's stats and prevents one-hit KOs.

evidence.quote: Your reward for beating him is the Jinx Belt, which in addition to boosting a character's stats also prevents one-hit KOs.

facts.subject: Jinx dojo sign
facts.text: After beating Jinx, the dojo sign changes from "J" to "M".

evidence.quote: The sign outside the dojo will also change from "J" to "M" in acknowledgment of Mario's fighting prowess.

facts.subject: Culex door
facts.text: The third door from the left in Monstro Town, right before the Item Shop, is sealed tight.

evidence.quote: notice that the third door from the left (the one right before the Item Shop) is sealed tight.

facts.subject: Shiny Stone
facts.text: Buy Fireworks from the guy in the house near the girl sitting by five crates in Moleville, then trade the Fireworks to the girl for a Shiny Stone.

evidence.quote: Buy some Fireworks from the guy in the house near where the little girl is sitting next to five crates. After, go talk to that girl and trade the Fireworks for a Shiny Stone.

facts.subject: Culex door
facts.text: Examining the sealed door in Monstro Town with the Shiny Stone lets you enter; save and prepare before entering.

evidence.quote: The Shiny Stone will react to the door and allow you to enter. Before you do, make sure you save your game and prepare for the fight ahead.

facts.subject: Culex
facts.text: Culex uses only physical attacks and a special move called Shredder, which negates attack and defense boosts such as Geno Boost, and has very high HP.

evidence.quote: Culex himself only uses physical attacks and a special move called Shredder, which negates any boosts to attack and defense, such as Geno's Geno Boost ability. He also has ridiculously high HP

facts.subject: Culex
facts.text: Zelikman strategy: Mario with Lazy Shell weapon and any armor or accessory that prevents insta-KOs, Peach with Lazy Shell armor, Bowser with a Safety Ring in the accessory slot.

evidence.quote:
Mario| Lazy Shell(w), any armor or accessory that prevents insta-KOs  
Peach| Lazy Shell(a) is the most important item here  
Bowser| Safety Ring in the accessory slot

facts.subject: Culex
facts.text: In Strategy One, use Peach as a healer and have Mario and Bowser attack normally; Bowser full-screen attacks can hit the crystals.

facts.subject: Culex
facts.text: Strategy Two party: Mario LV25-30 with Lazy Shell weapon, Hero Shirt, Safety Badge; Peach LV27-30 with Frying Pan, Lazy Shell armor, Safety Pin; Bowser LV24-30 with Drill Claw, Heal Shell, Jinx Belt.

evidence.quote:
Mario LV25-30| Lazy Shell(w), Hero Shirt, Safety Badge  
Peach LV27-30| Frying Pan, Lazy Shell(a), Safety Pin  
Bowser LV24-30| Drill Claw, Heal Shell, Jinx Belt

facts.subject: Culex
facts.text: In Strategy Two, use up Rock Candy, then have Peach use the Star Egg, healing her only when she is in the low 50s, and do not revive Mario or Bowser.

evidence.quote: Start by using up any Rock Candy you have, then continue the damage by having Peach use the Star Egg. Only heal her when she gets in the low 50s health-wise. Don't worry about reviving Mario or Bowser once they fall.

facts.subject: Culex
facts.text: Strategy Three: Mario with Lazy Shell weapon, any armor, Troopa Pin or Jinx Belt; Peach with any weapon, Lazy Shell armor, Safety Ring.

evidence.quote:
Mario| Lazy Shell(w), any armor, Troopa Pin OR Jinx Belt  
Peach| any weapon, Lazy Shell(a), Safety Ring

facts.subject: Culex
facts.text: In Strategy Three, keep using the Star Egg and Rock Candies, attack with Mario and Bowser, and use Peach to heal.

evidence.quote: Just keep using the Star Egg and Rock Candies, then whale on Culex with Mario and Bowser while using Peach to heal.

facts.subject: Quartz Charm

facts.subject: Beetle Mania

facts.subject: Beetle Mania
facts.text: You control a beetle along the bottom of the screen and shoot down turtle shells by firing stars with any of the four buttons (A, B, X, Y); if hit, mash the buttons to recover.

evidence.quote: Your objective is to shoot down the turtle shells by firing stars with any of the four buttons (A, B, X, Y) on the controller. If you get hit, rapidly mash the buttons to recover.

facts.subject: Beetle Mania
